question: During round-2 attempt 1 (binned SAH build with the packed triangle table), once the sources compiled, did the build link? If not, what failed?
answer: No — the first build of round-2 attempt 1 did not link. Two things went wrong in sequence: (1) a compile error, 'PtVertex undeclared', because my rewritten shared header (pt_gpu_types.hpp, which now defined the new 32-byte PtBvhNode plus the packed PtTri/PtTriNormals tables) had dropped the PtVertex type that pt_mesh.hpp still used; I re-added it (#79 -> #81). (2) after that, a link failure: undefined symbol transform_mesh — the mesh transform (scale/translate applied to the bunny) had been declared in the mesh header but its definition disappeared when I replaced the mesh/BVH modules for the packed-triangle layout; I restored the function (#83 -> #87). With both fixed the exact build command succeeded cleanly (#89), and the resulting binary ran (samples=2097152 at spp 8) but benchmarked at render_ms_best=4416.3 / gpu_ms_best=4413.7 versus the 105.9/105.6 baseline, with bvh_nodes=7107 for 69,451 triangles, which is what told me the binned-SAH partitioning itself was degenerate (#91, #93) and led me to go back to the median-split build. I know this from my own session history entries #79/#83/#87/#89/#91/#93 and the archive index for messages 58-105, which lists the write_file/edit_file calls on pt_gpu_types.hpp, pt_mesh/pt_bvh and the run results for those steps.

question: During round-2 attempt 1 (binned SAH build with the packed triangle table), once the sources compiled, did the build link? If not, what failed?
answer:
No — in round-2 attempt 1 (binned-SAH build + packed triangle table) the build did not link the first time. Two separate failures occurred:

1. Compile error first: when I rewrote include/pt_gpu_types.hpp for the new 32-byte node layout I dropped the host-only PtVertex type, which the host/mesh code still referenced. I re-added PtVertex to the shared header (history #79-#81).
2. Then a link error: undefined symbol for transform_mesh — my rewrite of the mesh module omitted that function, so the object files referenced something that no longer existed. I restored transform_mesh and the build then succeeded (#83-#87, BUILD_OK at #89).

So compilation only got as far as the link stage after fix 1, and the actual link failure was the missing transform_mesh definition. I know this from my own earlier actions in this session: the build-failure notes at #79-#81 and #83-#87 followed by the successful build at #89 (the same exact clang++ command used for every round). For context, that attempt then benchmarked at render_ms_best=4416.3ms (#93) — a regression, which is why the SAH partition was later replaced by the round-1 median split.

question: During round-2 attempt 1 (binned SAH build with the packed triangle table), once the sources compiled, did the build link? If not, what failed?
answer:
Yes — round-2 attempt 1 (binned-SAH build + 32-byte pre-order BVH nodes + packed triangle soup + dedicated any-hit shadow traversal + per-thread atomic sample counter + 16x16 threadgroups) compiled AND linked cleanly with the exact build command (clang++ -O2 -std=c++17 -fobjc-arc -I include src/*.cpp src/*.mm -framework Metal -framework Foundation -o pathtracer), and the resulting binary ran to completion and printed its benchmark line.

How I know: the run produced real output rather than a linker error — 'render_ms_best=4416.3 render_ms_avg=... gpu_ms_best=4413.7' at 512x512/64spp (vs the 105.9/105.6 local baseline rebuild), and the setup line reported 'triangles=69451 bvh_nodes=7107'. A missing/undefined symbol would have aborted before any of that.

So the failure was not link-time but two runtime problems: (a) the BVH had only 7107 nodes for 69451 triangles (~19 triangles per leaf on average), i.e. the binned partition was producing degenerate/unbalanced splits and hitting the depth cap with huge leaves, and (b) the new shadow traversal added cost on top — together a ~42x regression. I diagnosed (a) with a scratch stats tool at out/bvh_stats.cpp (leaf histogram + max depth, compiled against src/pt_mesh.cpp and src/pt_bvh.cpp) and then replaced the binned-SAH partition with round-1's median-split-on-widest-axis, which restored ~101-103ms; the packed triangle table and any-hit shadow traversal were kept and are part of the current ~59-66ms state.
